content: The Pettenkofer School of Public Health at LMU Munich, Germany, contributed to the evidence synthesis team for systematic reviews on the effectiveness of parenting interventions. Professor Frances Gardner, an expert in Child and Family Psychology from the Department of Social Policy and Intervention at Oxford University, United Kingdom, led this effort. Other key contributors from the same department at Oxford University included Ms. Sophia Backhaus, Ms. Moa Schafer, and Dr. Jamie Lachman. Professor GJ Melendez-Torres from the University of Exeter, United Kingdom, specializing in Clinical and Social Epidemiology, also participated. Additionally, Ms. Wendy Knerr, a senior researcher from The Write Effect in Oxford, United Kingdom, contributed to the reviews. The reviews on the INTEGRATE criteria for parenting interventions were also led by Professor Frances Gardner. Dr. Yulia Shenderovich from Cardiff University, United Kingdom, and Dr. Amalee McCoy from Oxford University, United Kingdom, were among the contributors. Ms. Moa Schafer, Ms. Mackenzie Martin, and Ms. Roselinde Janowski, all from Oxford University, also played significant roles. Ms. Sheila Varadan from the Institute of Private Law at Leiden University in the Netherlands and Professor Jane Barlow from Oxford University further supported the reviews. Professor Catherine Ward from the University of Cape Town, South Africa, contributed her expertise in psychology. The guideline methodologists included Professor Eva Rehfuess and Dr. Ani Movsisyan, both from the Pettenkofer School of Public Health at LMU Munich, Germany. The evidence gap map team was led by Professor Frances Gardner, with contributions from Ms. Sophia Backhaus and Dr. Jamie Lachman, all from Oxford University. The external review group included Ms. Yvonne Agengo from the International Rescue Committee in New York, USA; Dr. Betzabe Butron Riveros from the Unit of Family, Health Promotion, and Life Course at PAHO/WHO, USA; Dr. Chandre Gould, a senior research fellow at the Institute for Security Studies in Pretoria, South Africa; Dr. Patty Leijten from the Research Institute for Child Development and Education at the University of Amsterdam, Netherlands; Bernadette Madrid from the Child Protection Unit at the University of the Philippines; and Dr. Greta Massetti, a senior epidemiologist and branch chief at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention in Atlanta, Georgia, USA. The guideline writer was Ms. Sophia Backhaus from the Department of Social Policy and Intervention at Oxford University. The names and brief biographies of all proposed Guideline Development Group (GDG) members were published on the WHO Violence Prevention webpage for public consultation over a 14-day period, during which no comments were received. GDG members were required to update their Declaration of Interest before each meeting, and verbal declarations of interest were solicited at the beginning of each meeting. The declared interests of the GDG members are summarized in the document.
